method_card.title: School Life, Rules and Issues
method_card.content:
This lesson covers school facilities, uniform, school rules using se debe / se prohíbe / hay que, and issues at school such as bullying and stress.

SpanishEnglish
la bibliotecathe library
el gimnasiothe gym
la cantinathe canteen
el laboratoriothe lab
el patiothe playground
el uniformethe uniform
se debe + infinitiveyou must / one should
se prohíbe + infinitiveit is forbidden to
hay que + infinitiveyou have to / one must
no se puede + infinitiveyou cannot
el acoso escolarbullying
el estrésstress
la presiónpressure
el examenexam
aprobar / suspenderto pass / to fail (an exam)

Grammar focus — impersonal se structures: Spanish uses impersonal se for rules and prohibitions. Se debe + infinitive = you must (obligation). Se prohíbe + infinitive = it is forbidden to. No se puede + infinitive = you cannot. These are always followed by an infinitive — never a conjugated verb. Hay que + infinitive = one must/you have to (general obligation, no se).

Model paragraph: En mi instituto hay una biblioteca grande y un gimnasio moderno. Se debe llevar el uniforme y se prohíbe utilizar el móvil en clase. El acoso escolar es un problema serio porque causa mucho estrés.
(In my school there is a big library and a modern gym. You must wear the uniform and it is forbidden to use your mobile in class. Bullying is a serious problem because it causes a lot of stress.)
steps: Learn school facilities vocabulary with correct articles (un/una)
Master impersonal se rules: se debe, se prohíbe, no se puede — always followed by an infinitive
Use hay que + infinitive for general obligations
Practise talking about school issues using cause-and-effect structures with porque

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — school life, rules and issues appear every year

worked_examples.question: Translate: En mi instituto hay una biblioteca y un gimnasio moderno.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: En mi instituto = In my school. hay = there is / there are (one form for both).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: una biblioteca = a library (feminine), un gimnasio moderno = a modern gym (masculine). Note the article gender.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: In my school there is a library and a modern gym.

worked_examples.question: Choose the correct form: 'It is forbidden to run in the corridor.' — Se prohíbe correr or Se prohíbe corre?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: After impersonal se structures (se debe, se prohíbe, se puede), always use the infinitive.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Corre is the conjugated present tense (he/she runs). After se prohíbe you need the infinitive correr.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Se prohíbe correr en el pasillo. The infinitive correr is correct after impersonal se.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish school facilities to their English meaning
Match the Spanish school rule phrases to their English meaning

pairs.right: it is forbidden to eat in class

pairs.left: no se puede utilizar el móvil

pairs.right: you have to raise your hand

bronze.question: Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: una biblioteca grande y un gimnasio

gaps.correct_explain: hay = there is/there are. It does not change for singular or plural.

wrong.es: es means 'is'. Use hay to say what there is/are in a place.
wrong.tiene: tiene means 'has'. For describing what a place contains, use hay.

gaps.correct_explain: no se puede = you cannot. The impersonal se takes the singular form.

wrong.pueden: pueden is plural. The impersonal se takes singular → puede.

gaps.correct_explain: se debe = you must / one should. Positive obligation, followed by an infinitive.

wrong.deben: deben is plural. The impersonal se takes singular → debe.

bronze.question: What does 'Se prohíbe utilizar el móvil en clase' mean?
options: It is forbidden to use your mobile in class
You must use your mobile in class
You can use your mobile in class
You should use your mobile in class

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly says 'It is one o'clock'?

bronze.source_text: Mi profesor de historia es muy estricto pero justo. Las clases terminan a las tres.
model_answers: My History teacher is very strict but fair. Lessons finish at three o'clock.

silver.question: Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: Las clases empiezan a las ocho y
y terminan a las tres. Los

gaps.correct_explain: y media = half past. This is a fixed phrase for telling the time.

wrong.medio: medio is masculine. The time expression is always y media (feminine).
wrong.cuarto: y cuarto = quarter past, not half past.

gaps.rule: Days of the week — lowercase in Spanish
gaps.correct_explain: los lunes = on Mondays. Days of the week are not capitalised in Spanish. Los + day = 'on' (every week).

wrong.Lunes: Days of the week are not capitalised in Spanish → lunes.

silver.english: Lessons start at half past eight and finish at three. On Mondays we have Science.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Mi profesora de ciencias es más estricto que mi profesor de inglés.
silver.explanation: profesora is feminine, so the adjective must be estricta, not estricto (masculine).
silver.translation: My Science teacher (f) is stricter than my English teacher (m).

silver.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
silver.english: In my school there is a big library but there is no swimming pool.

distractor_labels.tiene: wrong verb — use hay (there is/are) for describing what a place contains, not tiene (has)

silver.source_text: In my school you must wear the uniform. It is forbidden to eat in the classroom. I find exams very stressful.
model_answers: En mi instituto se debe llevar el uniforme. Se prohíbe comer en el aula. Encuentro los exámenes muy estresantes.

model_answers: Mi instituto tiene muchas reglas. No se debe comer en clase y no se puede utilizar el móvil. Creo que el acoso escolar es un problema serio porque causa mucho estrés a los alumnos.

gold.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
gold.english: My teacher (f) is very patient and kind but sometimes demanding.

distractor_labels.profesor: wrong gender — the English says teacher (f), so profesora not profesor
distractor_labels.pacientes: wrong number — pacientes is plural, but one teacher needs singular paciente
distractor_labels.estricto: wrong word — estricto means strict, not demanding. Demanding = exigente

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are speaking to a visitor at your school's open day. They ask you about your school, its facilities and rules.

bullets.prompt: Describe what facilities your school has.
bullets.model_answer: En mi instituto hay una biblioteca grande, un gimnasio moderno y un campo de fútbol. Pero no hay piscina.
bullets.note: hay for existence, no hay for absence — hay does not change for singular/plural

bullets.prompt: Describe your school day — when lessons start and finish.
bullets.model_answer: Las clases empiezan a las ocho y media y terminan a las tres. Tenemos recreo a las once.
bullets.note: time expressions: a las + hour, y media (half past), es la una / son las + plural

bullets.prompt: Describe a school rule and say whether you think it is fair.
bullets.model_answer: Se prohíbe utilizar el móvil en clase. Creo que es justo porque los móviles distraen a los alumnos.
bullets.note: se prohíbe + infinitive + opinion with creo que

bullets.prompt: Mention a problem at your school and give your opinion.
bullets.model_answer: El acoso escolar es un problema serio. Hay que hablar con los profesores porque causa mucho estrés.
bullets.note: hay que + infinitive (general obligation) + cause-effect with porque

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Mi profesora de español es muy simpática y paciente. Es más divertida que mi profesor de matemáticas. En mi instituto hay un gimnasio moderno.
gold.correct_text: Mi profesora de español es muy simpática y paciente. Es más divertida que mi profesor de matemáticas. En mi instituto hay un gimnasio moderno.
gold.translation: My Spanish teacher (f) is very nice and patient. She is more fun than my Maths teacher (m). In my school there is a modern gym.

gold.question: Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: a las dos y los alumnos no tienen clases por la tarde pero

gaps.correct_explain: terminan is the ellas form of terminar. Las clases (plural) → terminan.
tienen is the ellos form of tener. Los alumnos (plural) → tienen.
los deberes = homework. Always plural in Spanish — never el deber in this sense.

gold.english: In Spain, classes finish at two and students do not have afternoon lessons but they have a lot of homework.
